assistant:
## What I found (the bottleneck)

- **Primary bottleneck is client-side video re-encoding** in `aimediatank-azure/src/lib/mediaCompression.ts`.
- The encode loop uses `requestAnimationFrame()` and **calls the `onProgress` callback every frame**, which (in the upload page) triggers **tons of React state updates** (`setUploadStatus`, `setUploadProgress`). That will peg the browser main thread and makes *everything* feel slow (buttons, admin UI, page navigation, media opening) while an encode is running or stuck.

## What I changed (immediate mitigation)

I updated `aimediatank-azure/src/lib/mediaCompression.ts` to:
- **Cap encoding FPS to 24** (instead of effectively trying to draw at display refresh).
- **Throttle progress updates** (only when percent changes, max ~4 times/sec).
- **Reduce MediaRecorder overhead** by using a larger timeslice (500ms vs 100ms).

This directly targets the “extremely slow interactions” symptom caused by main-thread saturation during video processing.

## Next highest-impact fix (if you want the app to stay snappy)
Even with throttling, **client-side full re-encode will still be heavy** for big videos. The real fix is to:
- **Move video encoding/cropping server-side** (job queue/worker) or
- **Run encoding in a Web Worker with `OffscreenCanvas`** + cancellation, so the main UI thread stays responsive.

If you tell me which deployment you’re using (`aimediatank-azure` vs `aimediatank-Vercel`) and where the Crop+encode is triggered in real usage (upload only? message modal? media edit page?), I can trace the remaining hotspots and wire in cancellation / “encode in background” properly.

user:
<user_query>
client side encoding is only one time for uploding, right? 
</user_query>

assistant:
Yes — **with the current code, client-side encoding/re-encoding only runs during upload** (when you call `compressMedia(..., 'VIDEO', ..., crop)` in `src/app/upload/page.tsx`).

A couple important caveats:

- **Only if you choose “Upload Edit” for a video**: that sets `videoCrop`, and then upload calls `compressMedia` with that crop → triggers the re-encode.
- **If you upload a video without cropping**: it still may compress/re-encode **only if the video is above the “skip size” threshold** (and in your `azure` version you also “never skip if we need to crop”).
- **The rest of the app (admin panel, browsing, opening media)** does **not** call `compressMedia` based on what I saw in `aimediatank-azure/src` (only `upload/page.tsx` and `profile/edit/page.tsx` import it, and `profile/edit` is image-only).

So: **it shouldn’t slow down the whole site unless an upload/encode is actively happening (or stuck) in that tab**. If the app is slow even when you’re not uploading, the next suspects are things like autoplay video behavior, heavy `fetch(...?t=Date.now())` no-cache requests, chat polling, or other expensive client effects.

### What was happening
- The admin Media table shows `-` when `fileSize` is `null` (or `0`), and **your DB has many records with `fileSize` not populated**, so the column stays empty.

### What I changed
- **Admin table UI**: display file size whenever `fileSize != null` (so `0` won’t show as `-`).
- **Admin media API (`/api/admin?action=media`)**:
  - When returning media rows, if `fileSize` is missing, it now **fetches `contentLength` from Azure Blob Storage** (`getProperties()`),
  - **fills it into the response**, and
  - **persists it back to DB** (best-effort).
- **Upload completion API (`/api/upload/complete`)**:
  - It now **prefers the authoritative blob size** from Azure (falls back to client size),
  - and **persists `fileSize`** so new uploads won’t be empty.
- **Backfill endpoint** (`/api/admin/backfill-filesize`) updated to persist using raw SQL as well.

All lints are clean now.

## Bug 1 verification

Yes, **the issue existed** in `src/lib/mediaCompression.ts`:

- `TARGET_FPS = 24` → `frameIntervalMs ≈ 41.67ms`
- On a 60Hz display, `requestAnimationFrame` ticks ~16.67ms.
- The condition `now - lastDrawAt >= 41.67` often triggers only every **3 ticks** (~50ms), i.e. **~20fps**.
- With `captureStream(24)`, this makes the stream capture frames when the canvas hasn’t changed → **duplicate frames / stutter risk**.

## Fix applied

I replaced the `now - lastDrawAt` gate with an **accumulator-based scheduler**:

- It accumulates `dt` each rAF.
- When the accumulator reaches \(1/24\) sec, it draws once and keeps the fractional remainder.
- On 60Hz, this naturally alternates **3 ticks (~50ms)** then **2 ticks (~33ms)**, averaging ~41.67ms → **~24fps** on average, reducing duplicates.

No linter issues after the change.

If you want, I can also add a small guard so we **always draw on the first frame** (right after `video.play()` succeeds), which can help avoid an initial duplicated frame at time 0.

assistant:
The admin Media tab **is** calling the right endpoint (`/api/admin?action=media`), so the “still `-`” means our Azure `getProperties()` is **not finding the blobs**.

### Why it was failing
We were using **one configured container name** (`AZURE_STORAGE_CONTAINER_NAME || 'media'`) for all lookups, but the blob URL itself encodes the real container:

`https://<acct>.blob.core.windows.net/<container>/<blob>`

If any records were uploaded under a different container (or the env var changed over time), `getProperties()` would 404 → no size.

### Fix I applied
I updated all size lookups to derive **container + blob name from the stored URL**, and cache container clients:

- `src/app/api/admin/route.ts` (admin list hydration)
- `src/app/api/admin/backfill-filesize/route.ts` (backfill job)
- `src/app/api/upload/complete/route.ts` (new uploads)

So now it will correctly call `blobServiceClient.getContainerClient(containerFromUrl)` per media item instead of assuming a single container.

No linter errors after the change.

If you want, I can also add a temporary debug return (counts of “size fetched / failed”) to the admin media response so you can confirm it’s actually reading blob properties in your deployed environment.

I found two big, concrete mobile slowdowns on the media page and fixed them locally (not pushed yet):

### What was making mobile slow
- **Video was auto-playing + looping on mobile** (`<video autoPlay loop>`) and we were also running an **autoplay-with-sound retry effect**. On mobile this often gets blocked and causes extra work/jank while the page is still settling.
- The media page fetch was **always cache-busted**:  
  `fetch(/api/media/:id?t=Date.now(), { cache: 'no-store' })`  
  This forces a full network round-trip every open, which is painful on mobile.
- The `/api/media/[mediaId]` endpoint was returning **full comments + ratings arrays** and doing extra DB work, even though the current UI **doesn’t render those lists**. That inflates payload + server time.

### What I changed
- `src/components/MediaPlayer.tsx`
  - **Disable autoplay on mobile**: `autoPlay={!isMobile}`, `loop={!isMobile}`
  - **Don’t run the autoplay-with-sound effect on mobile**
  - **Use `preload="metadata"` on mobile** (faster initial page / less download before tap)
- `src/app/media/[mediaId]/MediaPageClient.tsx`
  - Removed the cache-busting fetch; now it’s just `fetch(/api/media/:id)`
- `src/app/api/media/[mediaId]/route.ts`
  - **Stop including comments/ratings lists** (keeps response lightweight)
  - **Parallelize aggregates** and make view increment **fire-and-forget** to reduce TTFB

Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The throttling logic aims to draw at 24fps to match the 24fps `captureStream`, but on standard 60Hz displays, `requestAnimationFrame` fires every ~16.67ms. The condition `now - lastDrawAt >= frameIntervalMs` (41.67ms) causes draws every ~50ms (about 20fps), not 24fps. Since `captureStream(24)` captures at a fixed 24fps regardless of canvas changes, approximately 17% of captured frames will be duplicates, causing stuttering in the compressed video output.

assistant:
Two things are very likely behind “mobile suddenly slow / media opening slow” after crop+re-encode:

- **Codec/container compatibility**: your client re-encode pipeline was **always saving as WebM** (`video/webm` + `.webm`) even on browsers that actually record **MP4** (Safari). That can cause mobile playback failures/slow retries and “crop not working” on mobile.
- **Mobile MediaRecorder limitations**: some mobile browsers don’t support the WebM formats you were requesting; the old code would still proceed and then mis-label the output.

### What I changed (fix)
In `src/lib/mediaCompression.ts` I fixed the video encoding output handling:

- **Prefer MP4** (`video/mp4;codecs=...`, `video/mp4`) before WebM in `preferredTypes` (best iOS compatibility).
- If **no supported MediaRecorder mimeType** exists, it **skips re-encode** and returns the original file (so uploads don’t hang).
- On `onstop`, the output Blob/File now uses the **actual recorded mimeType** (`mediaRecorder.mimeType` / chunk type), and sets the **correct extension** (`.mp4` or `.webm`).  
  Previously it always forced WebM regardless of what was actually recorded.

This should directly address:
- **“crop not working on mobile”** (it was often recording MP4 but being labeled as WebM)
- **mobile media opening slowness** caused by incompatible/mislabeled video output

+        if (updateData.popupButtonText !== undefined) updateObj.popupButtonText = updateData.popupButtonText
+        if (updateData.popupImageUrl !== undefined) updateObj.popupImageUrl = updateData.popupImageUrl
+        
+        const promotion = await prisma.promotion.update({
+          where: { id: promotionId },
+          data: updateObj,
+        })
+        
+        await logAdminAction(adminId, 'UPDATE_PROMOTION', 'PROMOTION', promotionId, updateObj)
+        return NextResponse.json({ message: 'Promotion updated', promotion })
+      }
+
+      case 'deletePromotion': {
+        const promotionId = targetId
+        
+        if (!promotionId) {
+          return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Promotion ID is required' }, { status: 400 })
+        }
+        
+        await prisma.promotion.delete({
+          where: { id: promotionId },
+        })
+        
+        await logAdminAction(adminId, 'DELETE_PROMOTION', 'PROMOTION', promotionId, {})
+        return NextResponse.json({ message: 'Promotion deleted' })
+      }
+
+      case 'togglePromotion': {
+        const promotionId = targetId
+        const { isActive } = data || {}
+        
+        if (!promotionId) {
+          return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Promotion ID is required' }, { status: 400 })
+        }
+        
+        const promotion = await prisma.promotion.update({
+          where: { id: promotionId },
+          data: { isActive: isActive ?? false },
+        })
+        
+        await logAdminAction(adminId, 'TOGGLE_PROMOTION', 'PROMOTION', promotionId, { isActive })
+        return NextResponse.json({ message: `Promotion ${isActive ? 'activated' : 'deactivated'}`, promotion })
+      }
+
+      case 'toggleGame': {
+        const { gameId, isEnabled } = data || {}
+        
+        if (!gameId) {
+          return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Game ID is required' }, { status: 400 })
+        }
+        
+        const game = await prisma.gameSetting.update({
+          where: { gameId },
+          data: { isEnabled: isEnabled ?? false },
+        })
+        
+        await logAdminAction(adminId, 'TOGGLE_GAME', 'GAME', gameId, { isEnabled })
+        return NextResponse.json({ message: `Game ${isEnabled ? 'enabled' : 'disabled'}`, game })
+      }
+
+      case 'toggleNavbarItem': {
+        const { itemKey, isEnabled } = data || {}
+
+        if (!itemKey) {
+          return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Item key is required' }, { status: 400 })
+        }
+
+        const item = await prisma.navbarMenuSetting.update({
+          where: { itemKey },
+          data: { isEnabled: isEnabled ?? false },
+        })
+
+        await logAdminAction(adminId, 'TOGGLE_NAVBAR_ITEM', 'NAVBAR', itemKey, { isEnabled })
+        return NextResponse.json({ message: `Navbar item ${isEnabled ? 'enabled' : 'disabled'}`, item })
+      }
+
+      case 'toggleBadge': {
+        const { itemKey, isEnabled } = data || {}
+
+        if (!itemKey) {
+          return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Item key is required' }, { status: 400 })
+        }
+
+        const item = await prisma.mediaBadgeSetting.update({
+          where: { itemKey },
+          data: { isEnabled: isEnabled ?? false },
+        })
+
+        await logAdminAction(adminId, 'TOGGLE_MEDIA_BADGE', 'MEDIA_BADGE', itemKey, { isEnabled })
+        return NextResponse.json({ message: `Badge ${isEnabled ? 'enabled' : 'disabled'}`, item })
+      }
+
       default:
         return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Invalid action' }, { status: 400 })

+import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
+import { getServerSession } from 'next-auth'
+import { authOptions } from '@/lib/auth'
+import { prisma } from '@/lib/prisma'
+import { BlobServiceClient } from '@azure/storage-blob'
+
+export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'
+
+function getAzureBlobClient() {
+  const connectionString = process.env.AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING
+  if (!connectionString) {
+    throw new Error('AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING is not defined')
+  }
+  return BlobServiceClient.fromConnectionString(connectionString)
+}
+
+function parseAzureUrl(url: string): { containerName: string; blobName: string } | null {
+  try {
+    const u = new URL(url)
+    const parts = u.pathname.replace(/^\/+/, '').split('/')
+    if (parts.length < 2) return null
+    const containerName = parts[0]
+    const blobName = parts.slice(1).join('/')
+    return { containerName, blobName }
+  } catch {
+    return null
+  }
+}
+
+async function requireAdmin() {
+  const session = await getServerSession(authOptions)
+  if (!session?.user || session.user.role !== 'ADMIN') {
+    return null
+  }
+  return session
+}
+
+export async function GET() {
+  const session = await requireAdmin()
+  if (!session) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Forbidden' }, { status: 403 })
+
+  const missing = await prisma.media.count({
+    where: { fileSize: null, isDeleted: false },
+  })
+
+  return NextResponse.json({ missing })
+}
+
+export async function POST(request: Request) {
+  const session = await requireAdmin()
+  if (!session) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Forbidden' }, { status: 403 })
+
+  const { searchParams } = new URL(request.url)
+  const limit = Math.min(500, Math.max(1, parseInt(searchParams.get('limit') || '200', 10) || 200))
+
+  const rows = await prisma.media.findMany({
+    where: {
+      fileSize: null,
+      isDeleted: false,
+      url: { not: '' },
+    },
+    select: { id: true, url: true },
+    take: limit,
+    orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' },
+  })
+
+  const blobServiceClient = getAzureBlobClient()
+
+  let scanned = 0
+  let updated = 0
+  const errors: string[] = []
+
+  const concurrency = 10
+  let i = 0
+
+  async function worker() {
+    while (true) {
+      const idx = i++
+      if (idx >= rows.length) return
+
+      const row = rows[idx]
+      scanned++
+
+      const parsed = parseAzureUrl(row.url)
+      if (!parsed) {
+        errors.push(`${row.id}: invalid url`)
+        continue
+      }
+
+      try {
+        const containerClient = blobServiceClient.getContainerClient(parsed.containerName)
+        const blobClient = containerClient.getBlobClient(parsed.blobName)
+        const props = await blobClient.getProperties()
+        const size = props.contentLength
+
+        if (typeof size === 'number' && Number.isFinite(size) && size >= 0) {
+          await prisma.media.update({
+            where: { id: row.id },
+            data: { fileSize: Math.trunc(size) },
+          })
+          updated++
+        } else {
+          errors.push(`${row.id}: missing contentLength`)
+        }
+      } catch (e) {
+        errors.push(`${row.id}: ${(e as Error).message}`)
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: concurrency }, () => worker()))
+
+  return NextResponse.json({
+    scanned,
+    updated,
+    errors: errors.length ? errors.slice(0, 50) : undefined,
+  })
+}
+

+  const formatBytes = (bytes?: number | null) => {
+    if (bytes === null || bytes === undefined) return '-'
+    if (bytes < 1024) return `${bytes} B`
+    const kb = bytes / 1024
+    if (kb < 1024) return `${kb.toFixed(1)} KB`
+    const mb = kb / 1024
+    if (mb < 1024) return `${mb.toFixed(1)} MB`
+    const gb = mb / 1024
+    return `${gb.toFixed(2)} GB`
+  }

[Thinking] 
### File size check frequency

Yes — **it should be a one-time operation**.

- **Best practice**: set `Media.fileSize` **once at upload completion** (using the blob’s `contentLength`) and store it in the DB.
- **After that**: the Admin “File Size” column should **only read from the DB** (no repeated Azure calls on normal admin/media loading).
- **Exception**: older rows that don’t have `fileSize` yet — you run a **one-time backfill** (`Backfill file sizes` button / `POST /api/admin/backfill-filesize`) to populate missing values.

Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The throttling logic aims to draw at 24fps to match the 24fps `captureStream`, but on standard 60Hz displays, `requestAnimationFrame` fires every ~16.67ms. The condition `now - lastDrawAt >= frameIntervalMs` (41.67ms) causes draws every ~50ms (about 20fps), not 24fps. Since `captureStream(24)` captures at a fixed 24fps regardless of canvas changes, approximately 17% of captured frames will be duplicates, causing stuttering in the compressed video output.

Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The `fileSize` field is defined as `Int?` in Prisma, which maps to a 32-bit signed integer with a maximum value of ~2.14 GB. For media files larger than this limit, the backfill code stores `Math.trunc(size)` without validating the value fits within the 32-bit range. This can cause either a `ConversionError` or silent wraparound to negative numbers, resulting in corrupted file size data. For a media platform that may host large video files, `BigInt` would be more appropriate.

Related files (could not be opened):
- prisma/schema.prisma (lines 91-92)
- src/app/api/admin/backfill-filesize/route.ts (lines 95-100)

+    throw new Error('AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING is not defined')
+  }
+  return BlobServiceClient.fromConnectionString(connectionString)
+}
+
+function parseAzureUrl(url: string): { containerName: string; blobName: string } | null {
+  try {
+    const u = new URL(url)
+    const parts = u.pathname.replace(/^\/+/, '').split('/')
+    const containerFromEnv = process.env.AZURE_STORAGE_CONTAINER_NAME || 'media'
+    if (parts.length < 2) {
+      const blobName = parts.join('/')
+      if (!blobName) return null
+      return { containerName: containerFromEnv, blobName }
+    }
+    const containerName = parts[0] || containerFromEnv
+    const blobName = parts.slice(1).join('/')
+    return { containerName, blobName }
+  } catch {
+    return null
+  }
+}

-  popupMessage    String?
-  popupButtonText String?   @default("Get Offer")
-  popupImageUrl   String?

-  createdAt       DateTime  @default(now())
-  updatedAt       DateTime  @updatedAt

+generator client {
+  provider = "prisma-client-js"
+}

+datasource db {
+  provider = "postgresql"
+  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
+}

+model Account {
+  id                String  @id @default(uuid())
+  userId            String
+  type              String
+  provider          String
+  providerAccountId String
+  refresh_token     String?
+  access_token      String?
+  expires_at        Int?
+  token_type        String?
+  scope             String?
+  id_token          String?
+  session_state     String?
+
+  user User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
+
+  @@unique([provider, providerAccountId])
+  @@index([userId])
+}
+
+model User {
+  id            String    @id @default(uuid())
+  email         String    @unique
+  username      String    @unique
+  password      String    @default("")  // Empty for OAuth users
+  name          String?   // Nickname (display name)
+  legalName     String?   // Legal/full name
+  avatar        String?
+  bio           String?
+  phone         String?
+  location      String?
+  role          String    @default("VIEWER")
+  membershipType String   @default("VIEWER")  // "VIEWER", "BASIC", "PREMIUM"
+  membershipExpiresAt DateTime?
+  stripeCustomerId String?
+  stripeSubscriptionId String?
+  freeUploadsUsed Int      @default(0)      // Track free uploads used this period
+  freeUploadsResetAt DateTime?              // When to reset free upload count
+  paidUploadCredits Int     @default(0)      // Paid upload credits from Stripe payments
+  emailVerified Boolean   @default(false)
+  verificationToken String?
+  verificationExpires DateTime?
+  policyAgreedAt DateTime?  // When user agreed to Terms of Service and Privacy Policy
+  
+  // Admin moderation fields
+  isSuspended   Boolean   @default(false)    // Account suspended
+  suspendedAt   DateTime?                     // When suspended
+  suspendedUntil DateTime?                    // Suspension end date (null = permanent)
+  suspendReason String?                       // Reason for suspension
+  warningCount  Int       @default(0)         // Number of warnings received
+  lastWarningAt DateTime?                     // Last warning date
+  lastWarningReason String?                   // Last warning reason
+  bonusCredits  Int       @default(0)         // Bonus credits given by admin
+  creditsUsed   Int       @default(0)         // Total credits consumed (for display)
+  adminNotes    String?                       // Internal admin notes
+  
+  createdAt     DateTime  @default(now())
+  updatedAt     DateTime  @updatedAt
+
+  // Relations
+  accounts      Account[]
+  media         Media[]
+  comments      Comment[]
+  ratings       Rating[]
+  sentMessages  Message[] @relation("SentMessages")
+  receivedMessages Message[] @relation("ReceivedMessages")
+  reports       Report[]
+  purchases     Purchase[] @relation("Purchases")
+  savedMedia    SavedMedia[]
+  notifications Notification[]
+  chatMessages  ChatMessage[]
+  pendingUploads PendingUpload[]
+  conversationMemberships ConversationMember[]
+  creditHistory CreditHistory[]
+}
+
+model Media {
+  id            String    @id @default(uuid())
+  title         String
+  description   String?
+  type          String
+  url           String
+  fileSize      BigInt?   // bytes (from blob properties)
+  thumbnailUrl  String?
+  aiTool        String?
+  realDevice    String?
+  aiPrompt      String?
+  price         Float?    // null = free, otherwise price in USD
+  views         Int       @default(0)
+  isPublic      Boolean   @default(true)
+  isApproved    Boolean   @default(true)
+  isSold        Boolean   @default(false)  // true after purchased & downloaded
+  soldAt        DateTime?                  // when item was sold/downloaded
+  deleteAfter   DateTime?                  // scheduled deletion date (10 days after download)
+  ageRestriction String   @default("ALL")  // "ALL" = all ages, "18+" = adults only
+  
+  // Soft delete fields (content hidden but record kept)
+  isDeleted     Boolean   @default(false)
+  deletedAt     DateTime?
+  deletedBy     String?   // Admin ID who deleted
+  deletionReason String?  // Reason for deletion
+  
+  createdAt     DateTime  @default(now())
+  updatedAt     DateTime  @updatedAt
+
+  // Relations
+  userId        String
+  user          User      @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
+  comments      Comment[]
+  ratings       Rating[]
+  reports       Report[]
+  purchases     Purchase[]
+  savedBy       SavedMedia[]
+
+  @@index([userId])
+  @@index([type])
+  @@index([views])
+  @@index([createdAt])
+  @@index([isSold])
+  @@index([deleteAfter])
+  @@index([isDeleted])
+}
+
+model Comment {

+  // Relations

+  mediaId       String
+  media         Media     @relation(fields: [mediaId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
+
+  @@index([mediaId])
+  @@index([userId])

Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The throttling logic aims to draw at 24fps to match the 24fps `captureStream`, but on standard 60Hz displays, `requestAnimationFrame` fires every ~16.67ms. The condition `now - lastDrawAt >= frameIntervalMs` (41.67ms) causes draws every ~50ms (about 20fps), not 24fps. Since `captureStream(24)` captures at a fixed 24fps regardless of canvas changes, approximately 17% of captured frames will be duplicates, causing stuttering in the compressed video output.

Bug 1:
The throttling logic aims to draw at 24fps to match the 24fps `captureStream`, but on standard 60Hz displays, `requestAnimationFrame` fires every ~16.67ms. Since `captureStream(24)` captures at a fixed 24fps regardless of canvas changes, approximately 17% of captured frames will be duplicates, causing stuttering in the compressed video output.

<user_query>
Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The `fileSize` field is defined as `Int?` in Prisma, which maps to a 32-bit signed integer with a maximum value of ~2.14 GB. For media files larger than this limit, the backfill code stores `Math.trunc(size)` without validating the value fits within the 32-bit range. This can cause either a `ConversionError` or silent wraparound to negative numbers, resulting in corrupted file size data. For a media platform that may host large video files, `BigInt` would be more appropriate.

Related files (could not be opened):
- prisma/schema.prisma (lines 91-92)
- src/app/api/admin/backfill-filesize/route.ts (lines 95-100)

</user_query>

Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The throttling logic aims to draw at 24fps to match the 24fps `captureStream`, but on standard 60Hz displays, `requestAnimationFrame` fires every ~16.67ms. The condition `now - lastDrawAt >= frameIntervalMs` (41.67ms) causes draws every ~50ms (about 20fps), not 24fps. Since `captureStream(24)` captures at a fixed 24fps regardless of canvas changes, approximately 17% of captured frames will be duplicates, causing stuttering in the compressed video output.

Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The throttling logic aims to draw at 24fps to match the 24fps `captureStream`, but on standard 60Hz displays, `requestAnimationFrame` fires every ~16.67ms. The condition `now - lastDrawAt >= frameIntervalMs` (41.67ms) causes draws every ~50ms (about 20fps), not 24fps. Since `captureStream(24)` captures at a fixed 24fps regardless of canvas changes, approximately 17% of captured frames will be duplicates, causing stuttering in the compressed video output.

<user_query>
Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The `fileSize` field is defined as `Int?` in Prisma, which maps to a 32-bit signed integer with a maximum value of ~2.14 GB. For media files larger than this limit, the backfill code stores `Math.trunc(size)` without validating the value fits within the 32-bit range. This can cause either a `ConversionError` or silent wraparound to negative numbers, resulting in corrupted file size data. For a media platform that may host large video files, `BigInt` would be more appropriate.

Related files (could not be opened):
- prisma/schema.prisma (lines 91-92)
- src/app/api/admin/backfill-filesize/route.ts (lines 95-100)

</user_query>

Since `captureStream(24)` captures at a fixed 24fps regardless of canvas changes, approximately 17% of captured frames will be duplicates, causing stuttering in the compressed video output.

+  const containerFromEnv = process.env.AZURE_STORAGE_CONTAINER_NAME || 'media'
+  const raw = (input || '').trim()
+  if (!raw) return null
+
+  // 1) Full URL (typical): https://<acct>.blob.core.windows.net/<container>/<blob>
+  // 2) CDN/custom domain URL (sometimes): https://cdn.example.com/<blob> (no container segment)
+  try {
+    const u = new URL(raw)
+    const parts = u.pathname.replace(/^\/+/, '').split('/').filter(Boolean)
+    if (parts.length >= 2) {
+      return { containerName: parts[0], blobName: parts.slice(1).join('/') }
+    }
+    if (parts.length === 1) {
+      return { containerName: containerFromEnv, blobName: parts[0] }
+    }
+    return null
+  } catch {
+    // Not a URL: fall through
+  }
+
+  // Allow passing a blob name or path (e.g. "uuid.mp4", "/media/uuid.mp4", "media/uuid.mp4", "uploads/uuid.mp4")
+  const noQuery = raw.split('?')[0]
+  const path = noQuery.replace(/^\/+/, '')
+  if (!path) return null
+  const parts = path.split('/').filter(Boolean)
+

+  if (parts.length >= 2 && parts[0] && parts[0].toLowerCase() === containerFromEnv.toLowerCase()) {
+    return { containerName: parts[0], blobName: parts.slice(1).join('/') }

## Why your **File Size** stays empty

Your `fileSize` only gets populated in **two** places:
- **On upload completion** (`/api/upload/complete`)
- **When you manually run the backfill job** (`/api/admin/backfill-filesize`)

If either of those can’t resolve the blob size (URL format edge-cases, Azure SDK failing, container mismatch, etc.), then `fileSize` stays `NULL` and the Admin table shows `-`.

## What I changed (to make it work again)

### 1) Made size lookup much more robust
- `parseAzureUrl()` now handles **full Azure URLs**, **CDN/custom-domain URLs**, and even **raw paths/blob names**
- Added a **server-side `HEAD` fallback** that reads `content-length` from the stored `url` (works when the URL is publicly reachable), so backfill/upload won’t be blocked by Azure SDK/env issues.

Backfill route changes:

```17:66:c:\Users\chong\AI Studio\aimediatank-azure\src\app\api\admin\backfill-filesize\route.ts
async function tryGetSizeViaHead(url: string): Promise<number | null> {
  const raw = (url || '').trim()
  if (!raw) return null
  try {
    const res = await fetch(raw, { method: 'HEAD', redirect: 'follow' })
    if (!res.ok) return null
    const cl = res.headers.get('content-length')
    if (!cl) return null
    const n = Number(cl)
    if (!Number.isFinite(n) || n < 0) return null
    return n
  } catch {
    return null
  }
}

function parseAzureUrl(input: string): { containerName: string; blobName: string } | null {
  const containerFromEnv = process.env.AZURE_STORAGE_CONTAINER_NAME || 'media'
  const raw = (input || '').trim()
  if (!raw) return null
  // ... URL + non-URL parsing ...
  return { containerName: containerFromEnv, blobName: parts.join('/') }
}
```

And the backfill now tries Azure SDK first, then falls back to `HEAD`:

```105:159:c:\Users\chong\AI Studio\aimediatank-azure\src\app\api\admin\backfill-filesize\route.ts
let blobServiceClient: BlobServiceClient | null = null
try {
  blobServiceClient = getAzureBlobClient()

  console.error('Azure client unavailable for filesize backfill:', e)
}

try {
  let size: number | null = null

  if (blobServiceClient) {
    const parsed = parseAzureUrl(row.url)
    if (parsed) {
      const containerClient = blobServiceClient.getContainerClient(parsed.containerName)
      const blobClient = containerClient.getBlobClient(parsed.blobName)
      const props = await blobClient.getProperties()
      if (typeof props.contentLength === 'number' && Number.isFinite(props.contentLength) && props.contentLength >= 0) {
        size = props.contentLength
      }
    }
  }

  if (size === null) {
    size = await tryGetSizeViaHead(row.url)
  }

  if (typeof size === 'number' && Number.isFinite(size) && size >= 0) {
    await prisma.$executeRaw`UPDATE "Media" SET "fileSize" = ${BigInt(Math.trunc(size))} WHERE "id" = ${row.id}`
  }
} catch (e) {
  errors.push(`${row.id}: ${(e as Error).message}`)
}
```

Bug 1:
The throttling logic aims to draw at 24fps to match the 24fps `captureStream`, but on standard 60Hz displays, `requestAnimationFrame` fires every ~16.67ms. Since `captureStream(24)` captures at a fixed 24fps regardless of canvas changes, approximately 17% of captured frames will be duplicates, causing stuttering in the compressed video output.

Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The throttling logic aims to draw at 24fps to match the 24fps `captureStream`, but on standard 60Hz displays, `requestAnimationFrame` fires every ~16.67ms. The condition `now - lastDrawAt >= frameIntervalMs` (41.67ms) causes draws every ~50ms (about 20fps), not 24fps. Since `captureStream(24)` captures at a fixed 24fps regardless of canvas changes, approximately 17% of captured frames will be duplicates, causing stuttering in the compressed video output.

<user_query>
Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The `fileSize` field is defined as `Int?` in Prisma, which maps to a 32-bit signed integer with a maximum value of ~2.14 GB. For media files larger than this limit, the backfill code stores `Math.trunc(size)` without validating the value fits within the 32-bit range. This can cause either a `ConversionError` or silent wraparound to negative numbers, resulting in corrupted file size data. For a media platform that may host large video files, `BigInt` would be more appropriate.

Related files (could not be opened):
- prisma/schema.prisma (lines 91-92)
- src/app/api/admin/backfill-filesize/route.ts (lines 95-100)

</user_query>

Since `captureStream(24)` captures at a fixed 24fps regardless of canvas changes, approximately 17% of captured frames will be duplicates, causing stuttering in the compressed video output.

Related files (could not be opened):
- src/lib/mediaCompression.ts (lines 365-370)
- src/lib/mediaCompression.ts (lines 207-209)

Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The `fileSize` field is defined as `Int?` in Prisma, which maps to a 32-bit signed integer with a maximum value of ~2.14 GB. For media files larger than this limit, the backfill code stores `Math.trunc(size)` without validating the value fits within the 32-bit range. This can cause either a `ConversionError` or silent wraparound to negative numbers, resulting in corrupted file size data. For a media platform that may host large video files, `BigInt` would be more appropriate.

Related files (could not be opened):
- prisma/schema.prisma (lines 91-92)
- src/app/api/admin/backfill-filesize/route.ts (lines 95-100)

<user_query>
Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The `fileSize` field is defined as `Int?` in Prisma, which maps to a 32-bit signed integer with a maximum value of ~2.14 GB. For media files larger than this limit, the backfill code stores `Math.trunc(size)` without validating the value fits within the 32-bit range. This can cause either a `ConversionError` or silent wraparound to negative numbers, resulting in corrupted file size data. For a media platform that may host large video files, `BigInt` would be more appropriate.

Related files (could not be opened):
- prisma/schema.prisma (lines 91-92)
- src/app/api/admin/backfill-filesize/route.ts (lines 95-100)

</user_query>

Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The throttling logic aims to draw at 24fps to match the 24fps `captureStream`, but on standard 60Hz displays, `requestAnimationFrame` fires every ~16.67ms. The condition `now - lastDrawAt >= frameIntervalMs` (41.67ms) causes draws every ~50ms (about 20fps), not 24fps. Since `captureStream(24)` captures at a fixed 24fps regardless of canvas changes, approximately 17% of captured frames will be duplicates, causing stuttering in the compressed video output.

<user_query>
Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The `fileSize` field is defined as `Int?` in Prisma, which maps to a 32-bit signed integer with a maximum value of ~2.14 GB. For media files larger than this limit, the backfill code stores `Math.trunc(size)` without validating the value fits within the 32-bit range. This can cause either a `ConversionError` or silent wraparound to negative numbers, resulting in corrupted file size data. For a media platform that may host large video files, `BigInt` would be more appropriate.

*** Add File: c:\Users\chong\AI Studio\aimediatank-azure\src\app\api\media\preview\[mediaId]\route.ts
+import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
+import { getServerSession } from 'next-auth'
+import { authOptions } from '@/lib/auth'
+import { prisma } from '@/lib/prisma'
+
+export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'
+
+export async function GET(
+  _request: Request,
+  { params }: { params: { mediaId: string } }
+) {
+  try {
+    const media = await prisma.media.findUnique({
+      where: { id: params.mediaId },
+      select: {
+        id: true,
+        title: true,
+        type: true,
+        url: true,
+        thumbnailUrl: true,
+        isPublic: true,
+        isApproved: true,
+        isDeleted: true,
+        userId: true,
+      },
+    })
+
+    if (!media || media.isDeleted) {
+      // Return 404 so the client can mark it as "missing" without leaking existence.
+      return NextResponse.json({ missing: true }, { status: 404 })
+    }
+
+    // Public + approved media is previewable without auth.
+    if (media.isPublic && media.isApproved) {
+      return NextResponse.json({
+        id: media.id,
+        title: media.title,
+        url: media.url,
+        thumbnailUrl: media.thumbnailUrl,
+        type: media.type,
+      })
+    }
+
+    // Otherwise, only preview if the signed-in user can access it (owner/admin/purchased/saved).
+    const session = await getServerSession(authOptions)
+    if (!session?.user) {
+      return NextResponse.json({ missing: true }, { status: 404 })
+    }
+
+    if (session.user.role === 'ADMIN' || session.user.id === media.userId) {
+      return NextResponse.json({
+        id: media.id,
+        title: media.title,
+        url: media.url,
+        thumbnailUrl: media.thumbnailUrl,
+        type: media.type,
+      })
+    }
+
+    const [purchase, saved] = await Promise.all([
+      prisma.purchase.findFirst({
+        where: {
+          buyerId: session.user.id,
+          mediaId: media.id,
+          status: 'completed',
+        },
+        select: { id: true },
+      }),
+      prisma.savedMedia.findFirst({
+        where: {
+          userId: session.user.id,
+          mediaId: media.id,
+        },
+        select: { id: true },
+      }),
+    ])
+
+    if (!purchase && !saved) {
+      return NextResponse.json({ missing: true }, { status: 404 })
+    }
+
+    return NextResponse.json({
+      id: media.id,
+      title: media.title,
+      url: media.url,
+      thumbnailUrl: media.thumbnailUrl,
+      type: media.type,
+    })
+  } catch (error) {
+    console.error('Error fetching media preview:', error)
+    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Failed to fetch media preview' }, { status: 500 })
+  }
+}
+
*** End Patch

Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The throttling logic aims to draw at 24fps to match the 24fps `captureStream`, but on standard 60Hz displays, `requestAnimationFrame` fires every ~16.67ms. The condition `now - lastDrawAt >= frameIntervalMs` (41.67ms) causes draws every ~50ms (about 20fps), not 24fps. Since `captureStream(24)` captures at a fixed 24fps regardless of canvas changes, approximately 17% of captured frames will be duplicates, causing stuttering in the compressed video output.

The `fileSize` field is defined as `Int?` in Prisma, which maps to a 32-bit signed integer with a maximum value of ~2.14 GB. For media files larger than this limit, the backfill code stores `Math.trunc(size)` without validating the value fits within the 32-bit range. This can cause either a `ConversionError` or silent wraparound to negative numbers, resulting in corrupted file size data. For a media platform that may host large video files, `BigInt` would be more appropriate.

Related files (could not be opened):
- prisma/schema.prisma (lines 91-92)
- src/app/api/admin/backfill-filesize/route.ts (lines 95-100)

</user_query>

<user_query>
Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The `fileSize` field is defined as `Int?` in Prisma, which maps to a 32-bit signed integer with a maximum value of ~2.14 GB. For media files larger than this limit, the backfill code stores `Math.trunc(size)` without validating the value fits within the 32-bit range. This can cause either a `ConversionError` or silent wraparound to negative numbers, resulting in corrupted file size data. For a media platform that may host large video files, `BigInt` would be more appropriate.

Related files (could not be opened):
- prisma/schema.prisma (lines 91-92)
- src/app/api/admin/backfill-filesize/route.ts (lines 95-100)

</user_query>

Mobile users see an unmute button that appears to work (icon changes) but the video remains muted.

<user_query>
Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The `fileSize` field is defined as `Int?` in Prisma, which maps to a 32-bit signed integer with a maximum value of ~2.14 GB. For media files larger than this limit, the backfill code stores `Math.trunc(size)` without validating the value fits within the 32-bit range. This can cause either a `ConversionError` or silent wraparound to negative numbers, resulting in corrupted file size data. For a media platform that may host large video files, `BigInt` would be more appropriate.

Related files (could not be opened):
- prisma/schema.prisma (lines 91-92)
- src/app/api/admin/backfill-filesize/route.ts (lines 95-100)

Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The throttling logic aims to draw at 24fps to match the 24fps `captureStream`, but on standard 60Hz displays, `requestAnimationFrame` fires every ~16.67ms. Since `captureStream(24)` captures at a fixed 24fps regardless of canvas changes, approximately 17% of captured frames will be duplicates, causing stuttering in the compressed video output.

Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The throttling logic aims to draw at 24fps to match the 24fps `captureStream`, but on standard 60Hz displays, `requestAnimationFrame` fires every ~16.67ms. The condition `now - lastDrawAt >= frameIntervalMs` (41.67ms) causes draws every ~50ms (about 20fps), not 24fps. Since `captureStream(24)` captures at a fixed 24fps regardless of canvas changes, approximately 17% of captured frames will be duplicates, causing stuttering in the compressed video output.

<user_query>
Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The `fileSize` field is defined as `Int?` in Prisma, which maps to a 32-bit signed integer with a maximum value of ~2.14 GB. For media files larger than this limit, the backfill code stores `Math.trunc(size)` without validating the value fits within the 32-bit range. This can cause either a `ConversionError` or silent wraparound to negative numbers, resulting in corrupted file size data. For a media platform that may host large video files, `BigInt` would be more appropriate.

Related files (could not be opened):
- prisma/schema.prisma (lines 91-92)
- src/app/api/admin/backfill-filesize/route.ts (lines 95-100)

</user_query>

Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The `fileSize` field is defined as `Int?` in Prisma, which maps to a 32-bit signed integer with a maximum value of ~2.14 GB. For media files larger than this limit, the backfill code stores `Math.trunc(size)` without validating the value fits within the 32-bit range. This can cause either a `ConversionError` or silent wraparound to negative numbers, resulting in corrupted file size data. For a media platform that may host large video files, `BigInt` would be more appropriate.

Related files (could not be opened):
- prisma/schema.prisma (lines 91-92)
- src/app/api/admin/backfill-filesize/route.ts (lines 95-100)

</user_query>

<user_query>
Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The `fileSize` field is defined as `Int?` in Prisma, which maps to a 32-bit signed integer with a maximum value of ~2.14 GB. For media files larger than this limit, the backfill code stores `Math.trunc(size)` without validating the value fits within the 32-bit range. This can cause either a `ConversionError` or silent wraparound to negative numbers, resulting in corrupted file size data. For a media platform that may host large video files, `BigInt` would be more appropriate.

Related files (could not be opened):
- prisma/schema.prisma (lines 91-92)
- src/app/api/admin/backfill-filesize/route.ts (lines 95-100)

</user_query>

Since `captureStream(24)` captures at a fixed 24fps regardless of canvas changes, approximately 17% of captured frames will be duplicates, causing stuttering in the compressed video output.

Since `captureStream(24)` captures at a fixed 24fps regardless of canvas changes, approximately 17% of captured frames will be duplicates, causing stuttering in the compressed video output.

<user_query>
Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The `fileSize` field is defined as `Int?` in Prisma, which maps to a 32-bit signed integer with a maximum value of ~2.14 GB. For media files larger than this limit, the backfill code stores `Math.trunc(size)` without validating the value fits within the 32-bit range. This can cause either a `ConversionError` or silent wraparound to negative numbers, resulting in corrupted file size data. For a media platform that may host large video files, `BigInt` would be more appropriate.

Related files (could not be opened):
- prisma/schema.prisma (lines 91-92)
- src/app/api/admin/backfill-filesize/route.ts (lines 95-100)

</user_query>

<user_query>
Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The `fileSize` field is defined as `Int?` in Prisma, which maps to a 32-bit signed integer with a maximum value of ~2.14 GB. For media files larger than this limit, the backfill code stores `Math.trunc(size)` without validating the value fits within the 32-bit range. This can cause either a `ConversionError` or silent wraparound to negative numbers, resulting in corrupted file size data. For a media platform that may host large video files, `BigInt` would be more appropriate.

Related files (could not be opened):
- prisma/schema.prisma (lines 91-92)
- src/app/api/admin/backfill-filesize/route.ts (lines 95-100)

</user_query>

+import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
+import { getServerSession } from 'next-auth'
+import { authOptions } from '@/lib/auth'
+import { prisma } from '@/lib/prisma'
+
+export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'
+
+type Preview = {
+  id: string
+  title: string
+  url: string
+  thumbnailUrl: string | null
+  type: string
+}
+
+export async function POST(request: Request) {
+  try {
+    const body = (await request.json().catch(() => null)) as { ids?: unknown } | null
+    const ids = Array.isArray(body?.ids) ? body!.ids : []
+    const cleaned = Array.from(
+      new Set(ids.filter((v): v is string => typeof v === 'string' && v.trim().length > 0).map((s) => s.trim()))
+    ).slice(0, 50)
+
+    if (cleaned.length === 0) {
+      return NextResponse.json({ previews: [], missing: [] })
+    }
+
+    const media = await prisma.media.findMany({
+      where: { id: { in: cleaned }, isDeleted: false },
+      select: {
+        id: true,
+        title: true,
+        type: true,
+        url: true,
+        thumbnailUrl: true,
+        isPublic: true,
+        isApproved: true,
+        userId: true,
+      },
+    })
+
+    const byId = new Map(media.map((m) => [m.id, m]))
+
+    const publicApproved: Preview[] = []
+    const needsAuthIds: string[] = []
+
+    for (const id of cleaned) {
+      const m = byId.get(id)
+      if (!m) continue
+      if (m.isPublic && m.isApproved) {
+        publicApproved.push({
+          id: m.id,
+          title: m.title,
+          url: m.url,
+          thumbnailUrl: m.thumbnailUrl,
+          type: m.type,
+        })
+      } else {
+        needsAuthIds.push(id)
+      }
+    }
+
+    if (needsAuthIds.length === 0) {
+      const missing = cleaned.filter((id) => !byId.has(id))
+      return NextResponse.json({ previews: publicApproved, missing })
+    }
+
+    const session = await getServerSession(authOptions)
+    const user = session?.user
+    if (!user) {
+      // For non-public media, do not reveal existence when unauthenticated.
+      const missing = cleaned.filter((id) => !publicApproved.some((p) => p.id === id))
+      return NextResponse.json({ previews: publicApproved, missing })
+    }
+
+    // Admin can preview all non-deleted media.
+    if (user.role === 'ADMIN') {
+      const all: Preview[] = media.map((m) => ({
+        id: m.id,
+        title: m.title,
+        url: m.url,
+        thumbnailUrl: m.thumbnailUrl,
+        type: m.type,
+      }))
+      const missing = cleaned.filter((id) => !byId.has(id))
+      return NextResponse.json({ previews: all, missing })
+    }
+
+    const [purchases, saved] = await Promise.all([
+      prisma.purchase.findMany({
+        where: { buyerId: user.id, mediaId: { in: needsAuthIds }, status: 'completed' },
+        select: { mediaId: true },
+      }),
+      prisma.savedMedia.findMany({
+        where: { userId: user.id, mediaId: { in: needsAuthIds } },
+        select: { mediaId: true },
+      }),
+    ])
+
+    const purchasedSet = new Set(purchases.map((p) => p.mediaId))
+    const savedSet = new Set(saved.map((s) => s.mediaId))
+
+    const previews: Preview[] = [...publicApproved]
+    for (const id of needsAuthIds) {
+      const m = byId.get(id)
+      if (!m) continue
+      if (m.userId === user.id || purchasedSet.has(id) || savedSet.has(id)) {
+        previews.push({
+          id: m.id,
+          title: m.title,
+          url: m.url,
+          thumbnailUrl: m.thumbnailUrl,
+          type: m.type,
+        })
+      }
+    }
+
+    const previewed = new Set(previews.map((p) => p.id))
+    const missing = cleaned.filter((id) => !previewed.has(id))
+
+    return NextResponse.json({ previews, missing })
+  } catch (error) {
+    console.error('Error fetching media previews:', error)
+    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Failed to fetch media previews' }, { status: 500 })
+  }
+}
